note: file by atom, read by technique — every entry in Techniques & Templates, keyed by technique id

used_in.implementation: g(p) = 0.5+0.5·cos(2π·|p−c|/pitch) for each grating; the floor keeps a base blue coverage so the field never drops to paper.
used_in.limits: Pitches within ~4 u of each other push the beat fringe past the sheet; equal pitches collapse the moiré to one ring set. Below ~30 u the rings alias into the screen.

used_in.implementation: Multiplying the two gratings gives a dot lattice where both are high and long beat fringes where their phases drift; nothing is drawn as a dot — the lattice is the product.
used_in.limits: knee_lo ≥ knee_hi inverts the smoothstep. gamma below ~0.8 fills the lattice to a flat tint; above ~2.5 the dots shrink to specks.

cutoff.note: red coverage below this prints nothing

used_in.implementation: Red coverage is a clipped gaussian of distance from the core; inside it the blue lattice overprints as a lighter pink, which is how the rings read through the red.
used_in.limits: gain above ~2 saturates the core to a flat disc; sigma above ~700 u floods the sheet and the blue lattice no longer reads through.

params.threshold: uniform random per pixel per ink
params.overprint: where both inks land: overCore pink in the field, overFar plum on lattice dots (product > plum_above) inside the core

used_in.implementation: For each device pixel: blue if r1 < blue_coverage, red if r2 < red_coverage; both → overprint; neither → paper tint. A 0.6 px blur softens the pixel edges the way the reference’s scan does.
used_in.limits: soften above ~1.5 px dissolves the lattice into tone; cell_px is fixed at 1 in this rebuild (a coarser cell needs a hash per cell, not per pixel).

used_in.implementation: Flat neutral paper fill; the print sits inset by 34 u on every side.
used_in.limits: Above ~120 u the margin crops the beat fringe at the left edge.

used_in.implementation: Flat paper fill; the print sits inset on every side.
used_in.limits: Above ~120 u the margin crops the stretched band.

params.knockout: each fill clears the same shape on every other plate unless overprinting

used_in.implementation: Every closed shape is filled flat on one plate canvas and cleared from the others (destination-out), so plates only overlap where an overprint is intended.
Each shape is stroked twice on the black plate: 2.2 u on the path, then 1.4 u on the path shifted by a seeded 0.6 u jitter, which thickens the line unevenly.
The shadow side of a shape is clipped and crossed by 45° lines at a 6 u pitch with a 12/4 dash whose phase changes per line; drawn on the black plate so it never slips.
Each color plate is composited with its own down-right offset before the black plate lands in register, so fills open a paper sliver on the top-left of the line and spill past it bottom-right.

Each plate canvas is drawn translated by its own vector; the keyline sits on all three plates, so the offsets show as colored fringes on every edge and the overprint of all three is the near-black line.
used_in.limits: Past ~8 u a plate leaves its keyline and reads as a second drawing. With all three offsets equal there is no fringe and the print reads as flat digital color.

used_in.implementation: A mid-tone is the plate ink drawn as a regular dot grid clipped to the shape; the dot radius is set from the requested coverage.

params.mottle: perlin fbm 3 oct, cell 120 u, ±3 % multiply

used_in.implementation: Cream flat, then a low-frequency perlin multiply, a 0.35 px blur for the scan, then mono grain over everything including the inks.
One caption centered under each object on the black plate; a sheet title at the top and a folio at the foot.

params.color: white or pale tint at 0.55–0.72 alpha

used_in.implementation: Three short captions in Inter at 22 u, set flat under the grain so the grain sits on the type too.

params.order: navy 0 · blue 0.10 · cyan 0.22 · white 0.34 · yellow 0.44 · orange 0.54 · pink 0.64 · magenta 0.76 · blue 0.88 · navy 1

used_in.implementation: ART.lut(stops) gives 256 colors; the shading pass indexes it with the environment coordinate t, so color is a function of normal direction only.

normal-shading.name: Normal-buffer shading of a swept slab

params.section: rounded rectangle 300 × 160 u, fillet 30 u, 56 points
params.tilt_rad: 0.5 about the screen x axis through y = 740 u
params.wobble: n += 0.20–0.22·sin/cos fields of period 260–420 u plus 0.06–0.08 at 90–120 u, then normalize

used_in.implementation: Vertices P = C(s) + a·e1 + b·e2 with the section basis rotated by the twist; normals from the cross product of finite differences; triangles rasterized with edge functions into normal + depth buffers; per pixel the reflected ray of the orthographic view picks LUT[t].
band = exp(−((|n.z|−0.34)/0.06)²) mixes the edge color in; spec = (n·h)^60 mixes white in; both read from the same normal buffer as the LUT.

params.multiplicative: ART.grain amp 0.10, pitch 1 px, mono:false, seed 303
params.additive: σ 14/255 per channel on the ground, hashed per pixel, seed 304

used_in.implementation: ART.grain multiplies RGB by 1 + 0.10·n per channel (visible on the chrome and the type); a second pass adds signed noise of 14/255 so the black ground carries grain too, as film does.

params.additive: uniform ±21·(1 − 0.6·L)/255 per pixel, mono, lag-1 correlation 0.25

used_in.implementation: One pass over the whole canvas after every panel is drawn: a mono additive noise scaled down with luminance (it reads in the black, thins in the pink), plus a small per-channel multiplicative term for the color speckle.
Multiplicative hashed noise, identical across channels.

Each word is filled three times in #FF0000, #00FF00, #0000FF with globalCompositeOperation lighter on a transparent layer, offset per channel; where all three overlap the sum is white, at the edges one or two channels show; the layer is drawn under the chrome.

params.small: Archivo 700, 30 u, 2 columns × 3 rows at x 660 / 840, baselines 372 / 402 / 432

used_in.implementation: line 1 is sized to 924 u (font-stretch is set after ctx.font, which resets it); the figure sits on line 2 flush right; the slab is drawn after the type so it covers the bottom of the headline as the reference slab does.

Each object is a top-face mask drawn in the plane transform; a column scan drops every boundary pixel whose +x or +y probe is empty by the depth, labeling right or left face, top always winning; later objects overwrite earlier ones.
used_in.limits: The drop is a column scan, so a depth past the gap to the object below it paints over that object’s top face. Shapes thinner than 4 px have no interior for the ±2 px probe and get no side faces.

params.yellow: top faces + corner wash + marker strokes

gain.note: yellow corner wash at its center

used_in.implementation: Face labels become three coverage rasters; each raster is colored mix(white, ink, coverage) on its own canvas and multiplied onto the stock in plate order.
used_in.limits: Keylines past ~8 u close the counters of the letters. The wash is one radial falloff from the lower-left corner; past radius 1.3 it covers the whole sheet and reads as a yellow stock.

used_in.implementation: Before coloring, coverage is multiplied by a blurred copy of itself so fills thin toward their edges, and by a slow perlin mottle; after coloring ART.grain runs mono on the plate and paper pixels are reset to white.
used_in.limits: floor + gain above 1 clips fills to full coverage and the edge thinning disappears. stochastic above ~0.7 breaks the keyline into specks. A mottle scale under ~20 u reads as a second grain, not as uneven inking.

used_in.implementation: Inside the top faces the pink plate is full except where an fbm field crosses zero: the core of the band is paper, the rim half-coverage, which reads as swirls.
used_in.limits: core ≥ rim removes the half-tone rim and the veins go hard-edged. Above scale ~100 u a top face holds less than one vein. One octave gives smooth contour lines, not marble.

params.diagonals: ±30° through the same lattice, 18.2 u apart along a vertical

used_in.implementation: Flat gray fill, then verticals and both diagonal families stroked in the grid ink at 16 % before any plate lands.
used_in.limits: Above alpha ~0.35 the grid competes with the keyline. Under a 14 u pitch the three line families merge into a gray tint.

used_in.implementation: Each panel starts as a canvas linear gradient; C runs from the panel top-left along 66° from horizontal, with knee stops so black holds to 0.15 and pink holds from 0.67.

params.shape: closed spline through 13 measured contour points, off-panel to the left and below
params.halo_strength: four source-over passes of the wide blur: 1 − (1 − h)⁴

used_in.implementation: The shape is drawn twice on padded offscreens: once in crimson and blurred wide (σ 110 u), drawn four times to tint the field; once in black and blurred σ 33 u, drawn over. The wide blur is the halo that reddens the gradient near the black.

params.arc: y = q + (x − cx(q))² / 2R, R 750 u, cx(q) = 217 − 0.8·max(0, q − 233) u (panel-local)
params.right_cut: e fades where x > 333 − 2·max(0, q − 296), over 150 u

used_in.implementation: Per pixel: solve q, the peak height of the arc through the pixel (three fixed-point steps, since the peak x depends on q); darkness = envelope(q) × a thresholded cosine of q whose threshold rises as the envelope falls, so the stripes thin to points where the window cuts off on the right; light stripes sit at the opposite phase. The layer is blurred 3.3 u.

params.fill: radial white → 0.78 gray at the shape edge, union by lighten

used_in.implementation: Four Fourier-radius blobs are filled with a radial white-to-gray gradient on a black canvas (union by lighten) at one-third resolution, blurred with σ = 46 u and read back as a 0..1 luminance field.
used_in.limits: Under σ ~15 u the edge profile is too steep for the ramp and the bands alias. Past σ ~110 u neighboring blobs fuse and the rim stop no longer closes. harmonic_scale above ~2 makes r(θ) cross zero and the outline self-intersects.

params.measured_edge_px: paper→blue 12 · blue→navy 12 · navy 20 · plum→red 25 · red→orange 15 (at 1200 px)

shift.note: slides the field under the ramp

contrast.note: scales the field around 0.5 before the ramp

used_in.implementation: Every pixel of the field is replaced by LUT[field]; the ramp is the only place color enters, so all four colorways share one field.
used_in.limits: The ramp is read at 256 levels; contrast above ~2 leaves fewer than 6 levels across the rim and it stair-steps. A shift past ±0.15 moves the paper stop into the blobs or the core out of range.

from.note: field value where the dark stop starts

used_in.implementation: The darkest stop sits just under the mid-point of the blurred edge, where the profile is steepest, so it occupies few pixels and reads as a drawn outline; the blue halo is the ramp segment just outside it.
used_in.limits: from must stay below to, and both inside 0.41–0.53 (the stops on either side). A band wider than ~0.07 reads as a dark fill, not an outline.

params.measured: high-pass std 3.4/255 on paper, 5.5/255 in the core

used_in.implementation: Multiplicative mono grain per device pixel, then a low-frequency perlin mottle, both on the whole sheet including the blobs.
used_in.limits: Grain above ~0.08 reads as noise on the paper and breaks the rim. A mottle cell under ~30 u reads as a second grain.

params.grain: mono, amp 0.05, pitch 1 device px, seed 12

used_in.implementation: Before the perforation punch the stamp layer is multiplied by a low-frequency fbm and then by ART.grain, so both tooth and mottle follow the stamp and stop at the bites.
Each pixel is multiplied by 1 + grain + weave, where weave is the product of two sine waves at the weave pitch.
used_in.limits: Above ~0.08 either one competes with the dots.

used_in.implementation: Two 1 u ink rules across the sheet; the caption is set right-aligned 12 u under the first rule, the two-line studio label under the second.
used_in.limits: Rules under 1 device px are drawn at 1 px. A caption past ~22 u collides with the second rule’s label on a narrow sheet.

params.shade: +3 % toward scuff color from v 280 to 580

used_in.implementation: Each panel is a union of rectangles (spine, face, flap, tab, rounded tuck) tested per pixel; the fill is the board color mixed 3 % toward the scuff color by a perlin mottle and a vertical shade, plus sparse one-pixel dots.

params.haze: continuous tint 0.14·exp(−d/3 u) + 0.12·exp(−dc/14 u) + 0.06·exp(−df/2.5 u) under the dots

used_in.implementation: A chamfer distance transform gives d to the silhouette; dc is the distance to the nearest convex corner or fold junction and df to the spine crease or flap fold. A pixel turns lighter where a uniform random is below the summed density times the patch gate, so the wear reads as clustered abrasion rather than a line.
Faint diagonal strokes in the scuff color on a separate layer, blurred 1.5 px, then composited so the edges are soft.

price.tear: jittered polygon, 2 u amplitude on the bottom and right edges

used_in.implementation: Each sticker is a filled path drawn over the worn board with its own drop shadow; the foil is 36 hue wedges on arcs under a radial highlight.

params.digits: JetBrains Mono 3.2 u under the bars

used_in.implementation: A white box, then random-width dark bars from a seeded sequence; the digit row is mono type below the bars.

params.headline: Archivo 700, 32 u, 4 lines, pitch 37 u, at (340, 322)
params.meta_rows: JetBrains Mono 3.6 u, two rows with boxed keys
params.spine: Archivo 700, 8 u, rotated −90° on both spines
params.marks: 4-point star, globe, QR block, star box

used_in.implementation: All lettering is live type in the three inlined fonts with invented plain words; spine text is drawn on a rotated context.

params.bites: 12 across × 17 down, one centered on each corner

used_in.implementation: The stamp is painted as a rectangle on its own layer, then a circle at every pitch step along all four edges is punched out with destination-out; the punched layer is the clip for everything on the stamp.

Inside the letter mask a dark base is laid first; then a 45° dot lattice is walked and each dot is drawn with radius and color taken from the texture value at its center, so light patches of the texture become large tan dots.

params.font: Archivo 900, wdth 62.5 (extra-condensed; substitute for the reference condensed serif)
params.cap_height_u: ≈ 215 (size fitted so the run is 1003 u)
params.overhang: run ends 40 u above the stamp top

used_in.implementation: The title is drawn once into a mask canvas rotated −90° about its start point; the halftone is composited through it with destination-in, then the result is drawn on the stamp layer under the perforation clip.
Two invented lines centered on a point right of the middle, skewed −12° to stand in for the italic script; drawn after the grain so the white stays clean.

params.project: sc = P / (P − z); sx = cx + x · sc; sy = cy + y · sc
params.order: sort by depth d = (z + R) / 2R, far first

used_in.implementation: 150 particles climb a helix (0.018 of the height per second) while the helix turns (0.22 rad/s); each is projected through a pinhole at 800 u and drawn as text, far to near.

params.no_color_depth: glyphs stay white; only alpha and size carry depth

used_in.implementation: Nothing is shaded: depth is the alpha ramp and the projected font size, so far glyphs are ghosts and near glyphs are ink.
Every glyph with i mod 18 = 7 is replaced by the next palette name, set in its lifted on-ink color at weight 500 with a depth-scaled glow; the animation names its own system.

params.orbit: · with ø every 6th, Ø at center

used_in.implementation: Each animation reads its marks from a short ordered list by index, so the field is typeset from a vocabulary rather than drawn from shapes; the helix list mixes 10 marks with 13 three-digit numbers.
The helix canvas is masked by an elliptical radial gradient so glyphs fade out toward the middle; the title sits in the hole with a wide dark text-shadow that deepens it.

params.input: mx = clientX / innerWidth − 0.5; my = clientY / innerHeight − 0.5

used_in.implementation: The pointer shifts the whole helix by at most 18 u × 14 u, eased at 4 % per frame, so the field drifts after the cursor rather than following it.
A 70 × 8 grid where one sine phase picks both the glyph (from a five-step ramp) and the alpha (by distance to a sine centerline), so a two-wavelength band of laminar glyphs rolls across the frame.
Eighteen glyphs along a line lit by the positive half of one traveling sine, so a soft blue pulse runs left to right behind a fixed ▸ head; it lives inline under a dialogue turn.
52 glyphs on a flattened ellipse, each with its own breathing radius and an alpha that peaks at the bottom of the orbit; the canvas is held at 30 % under a pull quote.

params.reduced_motion: draw once at t = now, no loop

used_in.implementation: One setupCanvas and one loop helper serve all four canvases; under prefers-reduced-motion the loop degenerates to a single still frame, so the page keeps its picture without motion.

params.source: Planck 3000 K, green dip .1 at 548 ± 48 nm
params.integration: 380–720 nm, 4 nm steps, Wyman–Sloan–Shirley CMF fit

used_in.implementation: For every δ from 0 to 1599 nm the transmitted spectrum sin²(πδ/λ)·S(λ) is integrated against the color-matching functions; the 1600 colors are the LUT the field is shaded with. Order 1 (0–560 nm) is where the plates live: black → gray → warm white → amber → orange → red; the mauve and blue of 560–700 are the cool lanes.

params.sheet: δ = (d0 + A · sign(c)|c|^shape) · (1 + pin/r), c = cos(k · θw + ph + flow · t); shape for the peaks (blue), shapeN for the dips (pale) — the pale lanes are the narrow ones
params.radial: + rad · r — orange near the focus, red far out
params.load: δ = K · |σ1 − σ2| from Σ Flamant point loads (σr = −2F cos(θ−α)/(π r^decay)) + a uniform stress
params.biaxial: δ = d0 + c · |p − A| · |p − B| (Cassini ovals)
params.ribbon: δ = d0 + A · tanh(d / period) — a ramp across the ribbon: white, orange, red, blue in order
params.ring: δ = d0 + A · tanh((r − R) / period)

used_in.implementation: Each family is one expression for δ. The sheet keeps δ in the orange-red most of the time (shape 2.4 dwells near d0) and dips to white or peaks to blue briefly; the load family is real plane-stress mechanics; the conoscopes are the textbook interference figures.

params.domain_warp: (x, y) += wa · noise2((x, y) · wf), 2-octave value noise, wa .1 W, wf 1.2; the same hash in JS and GLSL
params.sheet: ψ = θw + twist · r + spiral · ln r
params.load: ψ = ½ · atan2(2τ, σx − σy) (principal direction)

used_in.implementation: ψ decides where the isoclinics fall. The domain warp bends the sheet — the plates are not flat starbursts — and warping θ makes lanes of unequal width; neither breaks the physics because δ and ψ are still evaluated from one coordinate.

params.term: sin²(m · (ψ − β + skew · sin(ψ − β)))^sharp, sharp for the β arm and sharp2 for the β + 180° arm
params.circular: circ mixes toward 1 (a circular polariscope removes isoclinics)
params.note: m = 2 is the physical crossed-polar cross (four arms); the plates read as two arms, m = 1, one polarizer effective

used_in.implementation: Multiplies the whole image; the black wedges are not masks but extinction where the material axis is parallel to the polarizer. Spinning β sweeps them around the focus.
mix(floor, chart(δ) · iso, env): the load point is opaque, the far field sinks, nothing reaches 0.

params.hue_grade: after gamma, hues pulled .75 of the way toward 6° (warm) or 196° (cool), whichever is nearer; saturation × 1.4 first
params.bloom: highlights (brightness .8, contrast 2.5 → a threshold near L .4) blurred at σ .05 W and added at .4 — the glow along the hot edges
params.shoulder: x/(1 + .25x), then highlights above L .6 desaturate .85 toward a pink-white
params.measured: plates carry no yellow, no green, no magenta — the grade explains the absence; band means: (235,182,147) (232,143,94) (225,95,57) (185,53,40) red side, (165,196,199) (120,154,165) (79,105,116) blue side, white (222,190,184)

used_in.implementation: Applied to the chart once (1600 entries), so per-pixel cost is a lookup; this is the step that turns a textbook chart into the plate palette.

params.measured: p99 horizontal gradient 12/255 per px at 1600 px

used_in.implementation: One gaussian over the finished color image; blurring after the chart is what mixes neighboring lanes into the gray-mauve transitions.
Every motion is a physical control of the instrument: rotate the polarizer, load the sheet, turn the sheet.

params.subject: headland with a signal tower and sheds, sea, far ridge — generated, lit from the left

res.note: source resolution as a fraction of the sheet

used_in.implementation: Sky, ridge, headland and sea are evaluated per pixel from seeded Perlin noise; tower, sheds and boat are drawn as flat lit/shadow faces on top. The function returns a canvas; every later technique only reads it.
used_in.limits: Any RGB picture works in its place. Pictures with no smooth area above upper_v show no guilloche; pictures with no pixel inside the hue range print as one ink.

used_in.implementation: Luminance is exposed and stretched about mid-gray before it sets any line width, so paper and solid shadow are reached inside the picture, not only at its extremes.
used_in.limits: Contrast above ~2 clips most of the sheet to paper or solid line; the swelling line then reads as a two-level threshold.

amp_pitches.note: phase shift in pitches at flow = 1 for a black-to-white step

used_in.implementation: A quarter-resolution copy of the picture is blurred; its luminance is added to the line phase, so lines rise over light forms and sink into dark ones. The same pass stores blurred edge energy for the guilloche mask.
used_in.limits: flow · amp_pitches · pitch must stay under ~1.5 × radius or neighboring lines fold over each other at hard edges.

pitch_u.note: reference: 3.2 px on its own image; 6 u resolves at plate size

used_in.implementation: Distance to the nearest line center is compared with half the tone-set width and antialiased over one device pixel. In the highlights each line is cut into dashes whose fill falls with darkness, with a hashed offset per line.
used_in.limits: Under ~2.5 device px of pitch the lines alias into tone. duty_max · weight at 1 closes the shadows to solid ink and the crosshatch has nothing to cross.

used_in.implementation: A second, unwarped line set whose width ramps from 0 at start to duty_max · strength at full darkness; the two sets are combined as 1 − (1−a)(1−b).
used_in.limits: start under ~0.35 puts hatch into the midtones and the picture reads as a net, not an engraving.

curvature.note: max slope of the wave; amplitude = curvature · scale / 2π

tone.note: how much darkness thickens the guilloche line

drift.note: phase wander of family A down the sheet

shear.note: family B phase advance per unit y, in units of 2π/S — tilts the braid so it does not stripe

params.lines: A: y + a·sin(2πx/S + drift·sin(2πy/2.3S)) = k·pitch;  B: y − a·sin(2πx/S + shear·2πy/S + 1.1) = k·pitch

used_in.implementation: Two families of stacked sine lines, mirrored, give the braided cells. Vertical distance is divided by √(1 + slope²) so line width stays even on the steep parts. The mask is (above upper_v) × (edge energy low); the straight lines fade by the same mask.
used_in.limits: curvature above ~3 makes the wave steeper than the antialiasing estimate holds; pitch near the main pitch makes the hand-over at upper_v invisible.

hue-key.name: Kept hue as a second ink

params.mode: variant.accent — "hue": ink takes each pixel’s own hue · "#hex": one custom ink · "off": monochrome

used_in.implementation: Mask = 1 inside tolerance of the chosen hue, feathered to 0, gated by saturation, scaled by strength and pulled back toward the main ink in the shadows by keep_shadows. It changes ink color only — line width is unchanged.
used_in.limits: tolerance + feather above ~90° keys most warm pictures whole; min_sat under ~8 % keys neutral grays by their noise hue.

cell_u.note: grain cell; one device pixel at the default

used_in.implementation: One multiplicative monochrome noise pass over paper and ink together, on cells of 1.4 u with lag-1 correlation.
used_in.limits: Above ~0.06 the grain reads before the line; this pass is the last thing to add and the first to remove.

spacing.note: lobe centers sit this many radii apart

child.note: chance that a lobe carries a smaller lobe on its rim

used_in.implementation: A bank is a row of circles along a spine plus the area under the spine. The depth of a point is its distance inside the nearest lobe; the shading reads that depth.
used_in.limits: spacing above ~1.9 opens gaps between lobes and the edge reads as beads. R_var above ~0.6 makes single lobes swallow their neighbors.

swell.note: a dot grows with tone, up to radius × (1 + swell)

params.rows: alternate rows are offset by half the pitch

used_in.implementation: One dot per lattice cell, moved by up to 0.42 of the pitch, with one random threshold. A dot is drawn when its threshold is under the tone at its position.
used_in.limits: radius above ~0.45 × pitch merges dots into a tint. jitter 0 shows the lattice as rows. Below 3 u pitch the sheet carries over 150 k dots.

rim_floor.note: tone left deep inside a rim bank

body_from.note: depth where a body bank starts to take tone, in lobe radii

used_in.implementation: Rim banks: tone = floor + (1 − floor)·exp(−depth / rim depth). Body banks: tone = smoothstep(depth) × wisp, where wisp is three-octave noise sampled in coordinates turned to the bank and stretched along it.
used_in.limits: wisp_mix at 0 leaves only the depth ramp and the banks read as flat steps. stretch above ~6 turns wisps into stripes.

grain.note: 1 = single on/off pixels; 0 = a smooth gradient

res_div.note: the tone field is sampled at 1/res_div size

used_in.implementation: The tone field is sampled at quarter size. Each pixel of the bank takes the wash color with a chance equal to tone × amount, so the gradient is made of single pixels.
used_in.limits: At amount 1 the wash hides the dots on light banks. grain at 0 gives a smooth gradient, which reads as blur beside the dots.

ray_floor.note: tone kept near the tip before the fade

used_in.implementation: Tone is the larger of a soft core disc and the nearest ray. A ray is a gaussian across its axis whose width tapers to the tip.
used_in.limits: Over ~60 rays, or a root width above ~140 u, the rays merge into a disc. core_radius at 0 leaves the rays unjoined.

swing.note: turns and scales the pulls through one cycle; Motion runs it

pull_u.note: a fifth pull, away from the sheet center; Live sets it at the pointer

used_in.implementation: Each pixel is sampled at its own position minus every pull vector times exp(−d² / r²). The grid is read at the sample point, so the sheet stretches behind a pull and bunches ahead of it.
used_in.limits: A pull folds the sheet when 0.86 × vector length exceeds its radius; at strength 1 the largest ratio is 0.65. Pitch under ~24 u puts a cell below ten pixels and the outline closes.

cell_at.note: edge of the solid cell, in cell units

edge.note: width over which coverage ramps at every edge

used_in.implementation: The distance from the cell center is a superellipse. Three shapes are read from it: the solid cell, an outline band, and the gutter past it.
used_in.limits: cell_at above gutter_at removes the stock band between a cell and its gutter. edge above ~0.2 thins every shape to a haze.

cell_var.note: how much strength varies cell to cell

drift.note: moves every pool once around a small loop; Motion runs it

used_in.implementation: Each pool has an ink, a center, a gaussian radius and a mode. Its strength is 2.4 × the gaussian, read per pixel and clipped at 1, so the middle of a pool is solid; the mode says which shape of the cell it colors.
used_in.limits: size above ~2 merges the pools into one field and no region reads. gain under ~0.4 leaves only the stray pixels.

stray.note: share of pixels near a pool that take its ink regardless

soften_px.note: blur after printing; 0 keeps single pixels

used_in.implementation: Per pixel: ink if a random number is under the coverage, with the ink drawn in proportion to each pool’s share; otherwise stock, or a stray ink pixel.
used_in.limits: stray above ~0.25 lifts the stock to a tint. Any soften above 0 turns the pixels into tone and the print reads as blurred.

used_in.implementation: Each meridian is an ellipse with the sphere radius as its tall axis and radius·|sin λ| as its wide one, stroked with a 6 on 5 dash.
used_in.limits: Over ~31 meridians the dashes of neighbors align into bands. A radius under half the sheet height shows the sphere outline.

trunk.note: control point distance, as a share of the reach

squash.note: vertical scale of the whole fan

sway.note: swings every bundle through one cycle; Motion runs it

pulse_s.note: time for a pulse to run a strand

used_in.implementation: Each strand is a quadratic curve from the hub. Its control point lies on the bundle’s ray at trunk × reach; its end is turned from that ray by the curl plus its share of the spread.
used_in.limits: trunk under ~0.25 lets strands separate at the hub and the bundle reads as a plain fan. Past ~24 bundles the sheet fills and single arcs stop reading.

params.stops: root tint at 0, second ink at 0.4, third ink at 1

used_in.implementation: A linear gradient from the hub to the strand end colors each strand through three inks; strands are composited with the lighter blend.
used_in.limits: With both alphas at 1 on a dark ground the whole trunk clips to white.

used_in.implementation: The strand layer is blurred and added back over itself.
used_in.limits: gain above ~1 washes the thin strands into a haze. On a light ground the pass is skipped: it would only gray the paper.

used_in.implementation: Square markers sit on bundle ends and on seeded free points; each carries a seeded number set up and to the right.
used_in.limits: Over ~60 nodes the labels overlap. Type under 9 u is unreadable at 900 px.

gap.note: gap as a share of the capsule length

fill.note: chance that a slot holds a capsule

fall.note: phase of the fall; Motion runs it

used_in.implementation: Each column is filled top to bottom with capsules whose length and width follow the column’s position t on the growth axis; lengths vary ±50 %. A column repeats every panel height, so the fall loops.
used_in.limits: Pitch under ~4 u turns the late columns into a solid tint. gap under ~0.1 fuses a column into a bar. A lean past ±30° crosses three columns and the axis stops reading.

floor.note: filled share of the height at t = 0

scatter.note: chance of a capsule above the wedge, falling with distance

used_in.implementation: The filled height is floor + (1 − floor)·t^power from the bottom; a few capsules are allowed past the edge.
used_in.limits: floor at 1 fills the panel and the wedge is gone. scatter above ~0.4 hides the wedge edge.

offset.note: slides the bands along the axis

width.note: gaussian width of each band in t

used_in.implementation: A capsule draws its ink from five gaussian bands along t. Each ink has its own layer; the layers are composited with the variant’s blend.
used_in.limits: width above ~0.35 mixes all five inks everywhere. Under ~0.05 the inks meet in hard stripes.

shape-mask.name: Shape clip with a masked edge

feather_u.note: width over which coverage ramps down before a clip edge; stippled fields only

params.shapes: rectangle · arch · ring with a gap

used_in.implementation: A field is drawn through a clip path. Three erasing strokes along the path then lower coverage toward the edge; the stipple turns that ramp into single pixels.
used_in.limits: A feather above ~20 u erodes a third of a narrow panel. On flat fields the ramp would show as a gray band, so it is off there.

density.note: share of pixels on at full coverage

fade.note: coverage lost from the head of a capsule to its tail

edge_u.note: blur of the coverage before the threshold; it dissolves the capsule edge

all.note: 1 = stipple every field in every variant

used_in.implementation: Capsules are drawn into a coverage layer per ink. Each pixel of the layer is then set fully on or off: on when a random number is under coverage × density.
used_in.limits: edge above ~1.5 u dissolves the smallest capsules. density under ~0.5 reads as a tint, not as ink.

node_u.note: diameter of the strand dots at mid depth

phase.note: turns the helix; Motion runs it

used_in.implementation: Each rung is a vertical capsule whose length is 2 × amplitude × |sin φ|. Two dots sit at its ends; the near strand’s dot is 45 % larger and the far one 45 % smaller.
used_in.limits: Over ~90 rungs the capsules touch and the helix reads as a ribbon. Under one turn there is no crossing and it reads as a lens.

turn.note: turns the dial; Motion runs it

used_in.implementation: Capsules point outward from a circle. Length and width follow a sine with three lobes around the dial; ink follows the angle through the five bands.
used_in.limits: Over ~120 spokes the inner ends overlap into a ring. lobes at 0 gives a plain sun.

used_in.implementation: Button, toggle, three chips, slider, pager and a nine-bar meter are all one rounded bar at different sizes, filled or outlined. The meter reads the slider value.
used_in.limits: Under 24 u height the 11.5 u label touches the pill edge.

scale.note: icon size as a share of its cell

params.set: arrow · plus · menu · signal · pause · check · sun · helix

used_in.implementation: Each icon is two to eight straight round-cap strokes on a 2 × 2 unit square; the last stroke takes an ink.
used_in.limits: stroke above ~10 u closes the gaps in the sun and the helix.

used_in.implementation: The clip path of a panel is stroked once over the field.
used_in.limits: Above ~3 u the frame competes with the capsules.

used_in.implementation: Capitals in JetBrains Mono, set letter by letter with 0.22 em added; a short rule sits one gap below the last line.
used_in.limits: Tracking above ~0.4 em breaks words into letters at this size.

used_in.implementation: A mono multiply grain over the finished sheet.
used_in.limits: Above ~0.06 the grain shows inside the flat inks.

seed.label: Seed
seed.note: every random draw in the effect derives from this one number

used_in.implementation: Die = an invented mark (compass, sun, crescent, knot, monogram), a word, or a ring seal, rasterized as an AA clip on the main thread (fonts). Die profile from the signed distance to the die edge (exact distance transform): a crisp shoulder, a straight wall over the die softness, a flat floor; lip = a narrow ridge just outside the edge. Height (CSS px) = stock height × (1 − crush · profile) − depth · profile + lip. The tooth flattens on the floor. Light: Lambert from the combined height + a height-field shadow toward the sheet light (the wall on the light side falls in shadow). Optional ink on the floor (film), so blind → letterpress is one dial.
used_in.limits: depth > 2 px: reads as a carved gouge, not a deboss. die softness < .3 px: walls alias. die softness > 5 px: the edge goes mushy. light elevation > 70°: a blind deboss vanishes under overhead light, by design

seed.label: Seed
seed.note: every random draw in the effect derives from this one number

used_in.implementation: Pressure = dropoff curve of the signed distance to a warped edge line (stroke direction, transition width), × the mask. Ink chain: the stock height under the inked area (blended with film-splitting noise, clumped and streaked along the stroke) is ranked to percentiles; pressure P inks exactly the top P of the surface, peaks first. Starve: valleys below the threshold never take ink. Wick: fibers carry ink past the edge. Mottle: paper formation thins the film. Film thickness thins with pressure unless the film breaks up; color = Beer–Lambert film in linear light. Light last: × the stock's shading. The ink sits in the tooth, not on top of it.
used_in.limits: transition < 4 px: reads as a hard vector edge: no run-out to see. break-up < .3: the edge becomes a gradient: the "AI gradient" failure. stock bite < .3: speckle stops following the paper and reads as digital dither. streak > 6: marks read as scanlines unless the angle is off-axis

Fibers: curved capsules at a count per 100 × 100 CSS px near the grain angle, raised into the height; pits: small depressions. Both also darken the albedo slightly. The same field is the stock for FX-01 and FX-02: its peaks take ink first, its valleys starve, its fibers wick. Mask = the sheet's cut or deckle edge; the sheet casts a contact + ambient shadow onto the page by the same light.

used_in.implementation: Motif = an invented mark, a word or a ring seal (AA clip, main thread) → exact signed distance. Coverage pattern: solid, or an analytic line / dot screen intersected with the motif (or with the sheet around it), so every line and dot keeps a 1-device-px edge. Film profile from the signed distance: a rounded shoulder (1 − (1 − d / rounding)²) rising to the film build. The film levels the FX-03 tooth: its top = lerp(tooth, smoothed tooth, leveling × profile) + build × profile. Stock: FX-03's relief and fibers under a board color (OKLCH; dark by default). Matte = Lambert from FX-03 × albedo + a weak, broad rough-dielectric sheen on the tooth facets. Film: Fresnel (n = 1.5, F₀ = .04) from a perspective viewer above the plate; the mirror vector samples the studio (a rectangular soft box at the sheet light, a dim ceiling, a dark room); gloss sets the box edge softness and the glint exponent. Under the film the matte sheen is gone and the stock is darker and deeper in OKLab (wet tone). One light: the box center, glint and FX-03 shading all follow FX.LIGHT.
used_in.limits: film build > 2 px: a blister or a sticker, not a print finish. edge rounding < .4 px: the sheen boundary aliases on 1× screens. pattern pitch < 2.5 px: lines and dots fall to a pixel checker at 1× (fine at 2×+). gloss < .35: reads as a matte or satin varnish: the mark stops revealing itself in the reflection. light elevation > 75°: the soft box moves behind the viewer: the film nearly vanishes (as real spot UV does under overhead light)

used_in.implementation: Motif → exact signed distance. Satin: centerlines across the motif at the stitch angle, one per 100 / stitch count px; each centerline is marched against the motif to find where the needle goes in and out (concave motifs give several floats per row). Ends stagger (alternating needle points + jitter); floats longer than the max split into rows at brick-staggered points. Each float: a capsule whose cross-section is rounded (flatter when long), sinking into its needle hole at both ends, with an S-twist ridge along it. Floats are z-buffered by height (neighbors overlap like real satin); an optional split, running or chain stitch is traced along the motif edge (marching-squares contour, real arc length) and laid on top. Cloth (FX-04 live): pucker ridges run along the pull direction at the stitch ends, decaying away from the edge; a crease dimples just outside the satin; needle holes darken it. Its own lighting is kept and multiplied by the pucker's Lambert. Thread light: Lambert on the thread normals + an anisotropic gleam (Kajiya–Kay along the twisted filament direction × a lobe across the cylinder), from the sheet light; a height-field shadow and cavity occlusion from the stitched relief fall onto the cloth and between floats. Color: OKLCH.
used_in.limits: stitch count > 45 /100 px: threads under ~2 px: the fill reads as a smooth sheet at 1× (fine at 2×+). stitch count < 12 /100 px: gaps open between floats. max float > 200 px: floats too long to hold: they would snag; read as a ribbon. sheen > .9 with low twist: reads as plastic. pull > .7: the ground reads crumpled, not stitched

used_in.implementation: Die = the same shapes as FX-06; foil lands on the AA die × the stock: valleys below the starve height release no foil (pinholes), edge flash breaks the boundary at the film-split scale. used_in.implementation: Site lattice at the pitch (CSS px), jittered. Value field (linear · radial · noise) eased from → to. Screen: FM keeps a site when its blue-noise rank < value; AM keeps every site with radius ∝ √value; the dial interpolates. The mask is sampled at the site, so dots are whole or absent. Each dot is geometry: a signed distance to an irregular nib outline (7 vertex radii), so its edge is always 1 device px of anti-aliasing, never a blur. The stock edits the edge: the distance is displaced by the stock height (edge rag), valleys inside the dot can starve, fibers wick a short way out. Film τ = thickness × pressure. Color: Beer–Lambert film in linear light (or a coverage mix). Ink B overprints by the same film product. Light last: × the stock's shading under the sheet light.
used_in.limits: pitch < 1.2 px: sites merge into flat tone at 1×: the stipple stops reading as marks. dot radius < .3 px: below ~½ device px at 1× a dot is a gray pixel, not a mark. dot radius > ½ pitch: dots fuse into a solid; FM loses its range. edge rag > .9 px: dots read as fuzz, not ink. selection white: clumps and voids at low density

used_in.implementation: Coating = brush strokes in stroke space (along s, across t): a load that runs out along the stroke; edges displaced by per-side noise (raggedness); a set-down pool and a drying rim; bristle streaks × the stock height decide where a dry brush still deposits. Thickness τ = load × unevenness (streaks + low-frequency drag) + pools; overlapping strokes add (a double coat prints deeper); paper valleys hold more sensitizer. Objects (procedural fern frond, grass with spikelets, or a cut-card motif) are an AA clip. Lift = a smooth field × the lift dial; contact sets how much lies flat. Shadow: for each lift level z the clip is sampled toward the sheet light at z · cot(elevation) (smeared ±20 % along the light) and blurred by z × sky scatter; each pixel blends the two levels around its lift. Exposure E = 1 − shadow × (1 − translucency). Develop: r = ((1 − e^(−2.2·exposure·E)) ÷ (1 − e^(−2.2)))^1.35, capped at 1.2; the coat saturates as τ' = 1.3·(1 − e^(−τ/1.3)); density = τ' × (a faint stain + r) × film density. Overexposure fills the penumbra in. Wash: unexposed coating rinses away; Prussian blue bleeds a little downhill into the whites, in streaks. Color = Beer–Lambert film of the tone (fresh, classic, peroxide-oxidized, tea-toned). Light last: × the stock's shading under the sheet light.
used_in.limits: object lift > 18 px: penumbra wider than the leaflets: the fern dissolves into a cloud. exposure > 2.5: penumbra fills in; fine pinnules and awns vanish. exposure < .5: pale, greenish print: reads as underexposed. raggedness > .8: stroke edges tear into islands. strokes > 6: brush marks shrink into stripes

used_in.implementation: Coating = brush strokes in stroke space (along s, across t): a load that runs out along the stroke; edges displaced by per-side noise (raggedness); a set-down pool and a drying rim; bristle streaks × the stock height decide where a dry brush still deposits. Thickness τ = load × unevenness (streaks + low-frequency drag) + pools; overlapping strokes add (a double coat prints deeper); paper valleys hold more sensitizer. Objects (procedural fern frond, grass with spikelets, or a cut-card motif) are an AA clip. Lift = a smooth field × the lift dial; contact sets how much lies flat. Shadow: for each lift level z the clip is sampled toward the sheet light at z · cot(elevation) (smeared ±20 % along the light) and blurred by z × sky scatter; each pixel blends the two levels around its lift. Exposure E = 1 − shadow × (1 − translucency). Develop: r = ((1 − e^(−2.2·exposure·E)) ÷ (1 − e^(−2.2)))^1.35, capped at 1.2; the coat saturates as τ' = 1.3·(1 − e^(−τ/1.3)); density = τ' × (a faint stain + r) × film density. Overexposure fills the penumbra in. Wash: unexposed coating rinses away; Prussian blue bleeds a little downhill into the whites, in streaks. Color = Beer–Lambert film of the tone (fresh, classic, peroxide-oxidized, tea-toned). Light last: × the stock's shading under the sheet light.

used_in.implementation: Scan lines at the pitch (≥ 2 device px), at the scan angle. Dose at a pixel = Σ over nearby lines of power ÷ speed × the beam's gaussian, integrated over the pixel (erf): anti-aliased lines at any angle. When the pitch clamps to 2 device px, the dose is scaled by the clamp so the tone matches a finer screen. Firing gate = the motif clip sampled at each line's centerline, softened by the spot along the scan; the head's turnaround adds dose just inside the edges it reverses at. Defocus widens σ and lowers the peak (same energy, larger spot): paler, softer, lines merging. A power ramp can run across the raster. Char = 1 − e^(−k·(dose − threshold)) → an OKLab ramp tan → brown → black, multiplied into the stock albedo (fibers char darker). Heat halo = the dose spread a few px, browning fibers first. Relief: ablation sinks the surface with dose; the tooth is burned smooth; a fine char crust. Lit by the sheet light (grooves catch it on one wall). Vector cut: a kerf along the motif outline (offset) or a tag; tabs leave bridges. The kerf opens onto the ground below, shaded by the card edge toward the light; its walls are charred.
used_in.limits: line pitch < 2 device px: clamped: finer lines alias into moiré on screen (dose is conserved). power ÷ speed > 1.4: char goes black and ablates; line structure survives only in the relief. defocus > .7: reads as a smudge, not a laser. halo reach > 9 px: reads as a scorch accident rather than a mark. kerf > 3 px: a slot, not a laser cut

used_in.implementation: Warp columns and weft rows at their own counts (threads / 100 CSS px); each thread: jittered center, thickness, dye-lot L, fray length, accent. Interlacing decides the top thread per crossing; a float is the run where it stays on top. Height = cylinder across the thread × arch along the float; under-threads sit low; hair = fine noise along the thread. Albedo in OKLab: under-thread, then top thread by AA coverage; accent as flecks (single floats, as in the source) or whole threads. Light: Lambert from the height gradient + a height-field shadow march toward the sheet light, so floats shade into the gaps; ambient occlusion darkens the gaps. Cut: the mask's signed distance plus each thread's own fray length, so threads end raggedly, not on a line. The swatch casts onto the page.
used_in.limits: count > 50 /100 px at 1×: threads under 2 CSS px alias against a 1× display: moiré (fine on 2×/3×). count < 18 /100 px: threads over ~5 px read as a woven-texture graphic, not cloth. fill < .5: reads as a grid of strokes, not cloth. fill > .97: gutters close; the weave flattens to a check. accent rate > .15: accents stop being accents

used_in.implementation: Warp columns and weft rows at their own counts (threads / 100 CSS px); each thread: jittered center, thickness, dye-lot L, fray length, accent. Interlacing decides the top thread per crossing; a float is the run where it stays on top. Height = cylinder across the thread × arch along the float; under-threads sit low; hair = fine noise along the thread. Albedo in OKLab: under-thread, then top thread by AA coverage; accent as flecks (single floats, as in the source) or whole threads. Light: Lambert from the height gradient + a height-field shadow march toward the sheet light, so floats shade into the gaps; ambient occlusion darkens the gaps. Cut: the mask's signed distance plus each thread's own fray length, so threads end raggedly, not on a line. The swatch casts onto the page.
used_in.limits: count > 50 /100 px at 1×: threads under 2 CSS px alias against a 1× display: moiré (fine on 2×/3×). count < 18 /100 px: threads over ~5 px read as a woven-texture graphic, not cloth. fill < .5: reads as a grid of strokes, not cloth. fill > .97: gutters close; the weave flattens to a check. accent rate > .15: accents stop being accents

weft.label: Weft count
weft.note: horizontal threads per 100 CSS px. Set it apart from warp for an unbalanced cloth

slub.label: Slub
slub.note: thread width variation along its length

hair.label: Hair
hair.note: fine fiber texture along each thread (linen is hairy)

wear.label: Wear
wear.note: probability a float is worn (thinned, flattened, faded) at the worn end

depth.label: Relief
depth.note: thread relief relative to pitch: how much the light models each float

twist.label: Ply twist
twist.note: the S-twist ridge along each float; it only appears once a thread is about 5 device px wide, so it matters in close-ups

diffuse.label: Diffuse share
diffuse.note: share of light from the sheet light vs flat ambient fill

shadow.label: Cast shadow
shadow.note: floats shading into gaps and onto under-threads, plus occlusion in the gaps

wC.label: Warp · C
wC.note: OKLCH chroma; reduced at constant L/h if it leaves sRGB

fC.label: Weft · C
fC.note: OKLCH chroma; reduced at constant L/h if it leaves sRGB

cC.label: Accent · C
cC.note: OKLCH chroma; reduced at constant L/h if it leaves sRGB

accent.label: Accent rate
accent.note: share of floats (flecks) or threads dyed the accent

mInset.label: Inset
mInset.note: distance from the plate edge to the mask edge

mAmp.label: Edge wander
mAmp.note: how far noise pushes the edge in and out

mScale.label: Wander scale
mScale.note: wavelength of the wander; small = ragged, large = drifting

mRough.label: Roughness
mRough.note: octaves of edge noise: adds fine teeth without moving the large shape

grain.label: Grain
grain.note: Size of one grain, in screen pixels. Every grain takes one color from a short ramp; 1 lays the ground at the screen’s own pixel, the page drew it at 2 on a retina screen.

speck.label: Speckle
speck.note: How far chance moves a grain along its ramp. 0 leaves only the light field and the brush streaks; higher breaks every tone into speckle.

fray.label: Bank fray
fray.note: How ragged the water’s edge is, grain by grain.

flowers.label: Flowers
flowers.note: Share of grains in the meadow patches that print as pink, pale yellow and violet flowers.

record.label: Riverbed glow
record.note: Share of grains over each strand of the record that print as its glow: green for yours, white for the model’s.

used_in.implementation: Ground and water are laid in as grain: every pixel takes one color from a short ramp, chosen by a field of light, a streak of brushwork and chance, so light blooms and falls off in speckle and nothing has a hard edge. The record lies on the bed as two kinds of glow.

width.label: Width
width.note: Half-width of the river against the height of the plate.

meander.label: Meander
meander.note: Depth of the river’s long bend.

sun.label: Sun along the river
sun.note: Where the light on the water sits along the current.

light.label: Sun on the water
light.note: Reach and strength of the bloom of light on the water.

used_in.implementation: One centerline with a slowly varying width; banks wander about it by noise; three islands part the current; a light field of broad sweeps, a worn path and a sun on the water.

grass.label: Grass
grass.note: Count of tapered grass strokes, leaning with the wind.

current.label: Current
current.note: Count of long current strokes that part round the islands, and of the glints running down the water.

bank.label: Bank line
bank.note: Weight of the broken dark line where water meets land.

used_in.implementation: Tapered strokes of a loaded brush over the grain: grass on land, current in the water, a dark line at the bank that thickens, thins and breaks.

speed.label: Speed
speed.note: How fast the river’s clock runs when the plate plays: current, koi, canoe, walkers, kite.

moment.label: Moment
moment.note: The time on the river’s clock the still shows, and where Play starts.

used_in.implementation: Everything that moves reads one clock: glints and koi ride the current, the canoe passes from one model’s reach to the next, people and robots walk the banks.

cell.label: Cell
cell.note: Side of one screen cell, in screen pixels. Held at this size at any plate size, so a larger plate prints more dots, not bigger ones.

dot.label: Dot
dot.note: Side of one dot, in screen pixels. Dots print as whole pixels; a fractional size is kept by thinning the count, so tone does not jump.

perCell.label: Dots per cell
perCell.note: Most dots one cell can hold. Tone is the count: density times this, the remainder kept by the hash.

jitter.label: Scatter
jitter.note: Where a dot may land in its cell. 1 is anywhere (the stochastic screen); 0 stacks every dot on the cell center, an ordered screen.

round.label: Round from
round.note: Dots this size and larger print round; smaller ones are square pixels.

seed.label: Seed
seed.note: Re-rolls every hash: which dots are kept and where they land.

used_in.implementation: Each cell of a jittered grid prints up to N dots at hashed positions and keeps the last one with probability equal to the remainder, so density is carried by the count of marks and nothing is blended.

gamma.label: Ramp curve
gamma.note: First figure: density = floor + (top - floor) · x^curve across the width.

gamma2.label: Split ramp curve
gamma2.note: Second figure: the same ramp, printed dark green over teal.

split.label: Split
split.note: Where the second figure turns from dark green to teal, with a hairline on the seam.

used_in.implementation: density = floor + (top - floor) · (x / W)^curve, screened by the counted screen; the split ramp prints the top in dark green and the bottom in teal.

pitchA.label: Pitch, you
pitchA.note: Ring pitch of the first source, in figure units.

pitchB.label: Pitch, Mir
pitchB.note: Ring pitch of the second source. Close to the first, the beat between them opens into wide lozenges.

gain.label: Gain
gain.note: Density at a shared crest: (0.02 + gain · (A·B)^1.25) under the falloff.

reach.label: Reach
reach.note: Width of the falloff that fades the rings toward the edges, as a share of the figure width.

peak.label: Purple peak
peak.note: Where both crests stand above this near the first source, the cell prints one purple count. 1 removes it.

used_in.implementation: Two ring screens A = ½ + ½cos(2π dA / pA) and B likewise; their product, under a gaussian falloff, is the density; the cell takes dark green where A leads and teal where B does.

tone.label: Tone
tone.note: Each letter prints its digit (1 to 9, from its place in the alphabet) as density digit/9 times this.

inset.label: Inset
inset.note: Margin of white inside each cell, in figure units.

used_in.implementation: The words are spelled one letter per cell; each letter maps to a digit 1 to 9 and the cell prints that count as its tone, in the ink of its channel.
